sections.html:
Calvert County fills a peninsula in Southern Maryland between the Chesapeake Bay and the Patuxent River, with Prince Frederick as the county seat. Water covers roughly 38% of its 345 square miles, and the county includes five islands, Solomons Island and Broomes Island among them. Many residents commute toward Washington, and household incomes are high, which keeps demand for houses steady even when a property needs work.

A waterfront cottage in Chesapeake Beach and a ranch house on a wooded lot near Prince Frederick can have little in common when it comes to insurance, septic and upkeep, so describe yours in detail.

The county rate is $0.967 per $100 of assessed value and the state adds $0.112, for $1.079 per $100 in unincorporated areas. The fiscal 2027 county rate stays at 96.7 cents, the same as the year before. Because assessments rose, some bills still went up with the rate flat.

The two bay towns get a lower county rate and then add their own town rate. If you are selling near the beach, look up the exact address in the state tax rate table, since the rates are summed by location.

Total full cash value rose 9.0%, from about $5.07 billion to $5.52 billion, and residential value rose 8.8%. Of 10,856 residential properties, 10,757 went up, which is 99.09%. Appeal to the state assessment office within 45 days of the notice date.

Under the homestead credit, taxable increases on an owner-occupied home are capped at 10% a year, effective July 1, 2026. You must apply for the credit. Increases in assessed value phase in over three years.

sections.h2: Billing, payment and the Treasurer's Office
sections.html:
The tax year runs July 1 through June 30, and owners of a principal residence can pay in two installments, September 30 and December 31. The second installment carries a service charge, so ask the Treasurer's Office for the amount. If no bill has reached you by August 31, request a duplicate. New construction is billed on a half-year basis from January 1 through June 30.

  • Online payments go through a vendor that charges 3.57% on cards, with a $5.18 minimum, or $2.59 for an e-check. The county does not keep the fee.
  • Partial payments are accepted only when the property is not in tax sale.
  • If a lender pays from escrow, forward the bill to the servicer and confirm payment on the annual escrow statement.
  • Address and residency changes go to the state assessment office, not the Treasurer.

The Treasurer's Office is at 150 Main Street, Prince Frederick, 410-535-1600. It handles tax liens and runs the annual tax sale.

sections.h2: Help for owners who are behind
sections.html:
The Homeowner Protection Program can pull a qualifying owner out of the tax sale process for three years. Requirements include a principal residence, an assessed value of $300,000 or less, household income of $60,000 or less, and non-dwelling assets of $200,000 or less.

The state Homeowners' Tax Credit is open to primary-residence owners with gross household income under $60,000, and applications go to the state. A Bay Restoration Fund hardship exemption lasts one year and must be renewed. These programs can lower what you owe before closing, and they can slow a tax sale long enough to list the house without a lien deadline hanging over you.

sections.h2: Building excise tax on new homes
sections.html:
Calvert charges a building excise tax on new residential construction, and it follows the property as a lien. A new single-family detached house totals $12,950, with $4,550 due at permit and $4,200 on each of the next two tax bills.

Other totals are $10,325 for a single-family attached unit, $9,050 for a manufactured home and $7,750 for an apartment. Later installments show up on the regular tax bill, so a buyer of a newly built home should ask whether any remain unpaid. The county enforces the tax like real property tax, with the same priority, interest and penalties for lien purposes. If you are selling a house built in the last two or three years, ask the Treasurer's Office what is left.

Routes 4 and 2 meet at Sunderland and run together as Route 2-4, Solomons Island Road, through Prince Frederick, St. Leonard and Lusby. Route 260 runs southeast to Chesapeake Beach, and the Governor Thomas Johnson Bridge carries Route 4 into St. Mary's County. Summers are hot and humid and winters mild to chilly, so roofs and siding see the full range, and buyers of bay-side houses will look closely at both.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call the Treasurer
sections.html:
• The tax ID number for your account, which the online portal uses to find your bills.
  • Your most recent bill, plus the one before it if a balance carries over.
  • Your mortgage servicer's name, if the lender pays from escrow.
  • For a newer house, the building permit date, so the office can tell you which excise installments are left.
  • Proof of income and assets if you want to ask about the Homeowner Protection Program or the state credit.

The office can tell you whether the account has been sent to tax sale. That single fact decides whether a partial payment is still possible, so ask it first.

Calvert's long shoreline means many sellers have docks, bulkheads, septic systems or houses close to the water. Buyers and their lenders ask about all of these, and a missing permit or an old system can slow a traditional sale. Collect whatever paperwork you have on repairs and upgrades. A cash offer is made on the house as it stands, so an aging septic tank or a tired deck is not something you have to resolve before closing, though the tax balance still gets paid from the proceeds.

1. Look up the account on the county's online tax portal using the tax ID number.
  2. Ask the Treasurer's Office whether any amount has gone to tax sale, because partial payments stop once it has.
  3. Check your mortgage escrow so you do not pay twice.
  4. Ask the title company to order a payoff through your closing date.

If the house also needs repairs you cannot afford, selling as is lets unpaid tax come out of the proceeds at settlement instead of sitting on the account. Call or text us with the address and we will tell you what we can offer.

faqs.q: What is the Calvert County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $0.967 per $100 of assessed value, unchanged for fiscal 2027. With the state's $0.112, unincorporated areas pay $1.079 per $100.

faqs.q: When are Calvert County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Owners of a principal residence may pay in two installments due September 30 and December 31. The second carries a service charge.

faqs.q: What is the homestead cap in Calvert County?
faqs.a: Taxable increases on an owner-occupied home are capped at 10% a year effective July 1, 2026, if you have applied for the credit.

faqs.q: Can I get out of a Calvert County tax sale?
faqs.a: The Homeowner Protection Program can remove a qualifying owner from the tax sale process for three years. The county sets income, asset and assessed value limits.

faqs.q: Does a new Calvert County house carry an extra tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The county building excise tax on a new single-family detached house totals $12,950, paid in three installments, and it is a lien until paid.
